ops.text: Two stacked traps in the fake-binary test fixtures bit the gt-lane push twice (2026-07-24): (1) macOS /bin/sh is Apple bash and silently tolerates bash-only expansions, so `${VAR_<operand>-}` eval'd with a slash-bearing branch name shipped green locally and exploded only on ubuntu-latest where /bin/sh is dash ("Bad substitution", exit 2) — first Linux exposure of the reviews fixture was the main push itself; (2) the obvious fix (sanitize via `tr`) hangs the whole suite locally because the test harness sets PATH to ONLY the fake-bin dir — no tr/sed/any external tool exists inside fake scripts, and the failure mode is an infinite watch loop, not an error. Fixture rule worth remembering (and maybe a capt-hook nudge on `*_test.go` heredoc shell): fake-binary scripts must be pure POSIX built-ins, and any var name built from runtime input needs a `case $x in *[!A-Za-z0-9_]*)` guard. Local dash exists at /bin/dash on macOS for verification.
